title: a tooth that needs what a box lacks prints NOTRUN, which is neither green nor red, and the box records no seal for it
intention: A proof tooth can print NOTRUN <name> with a reason when the box lacks what it needs (systemd, bubblewrap). teeth_printed returns it in a third list, never in green and never in red; a tester run whose every tooth is NOTRUN writes NO seal on that box and says it asks for the Linux sealer's; a run with some teeth green and some NOTRUN seals only the green ones and names the others. One marker covers systemd teeth and bwrap-only teeth alike.
why: Outline 9.4.2.3.3.1 (Akien, Q#90): one sealer, on cairn's home, Linux. 9.4.8.1 (CC's decision on Q#98): a tooth that needs what a box lacks reads not-run on that box, never red, its outcome the sealer's; a box without bubblewrap asks for the run and does not run it itself. Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell: that state is NOT BUILT. teeth_printed (proof_coverage.py) reads only GREEN_MARKERS and RED_MARKERS, and cairn/devices/tester/device.py lines 736-745 turn exit 0 with no named green tooth into RED ('zero teeth printed'), so a proof on Windows that cannot run has three outcomes: exit non-zero (red), exit 0 with no teeth (red by that rule), or print a green tooth it did not run (a false green). test_shim_starts_the_loop.py (d88887fbe31e) is the measured case, an honest named red as an interim.
traces_to: Law 3 (an unmeasured claim is labeled), Law 8 (a hollow green is worse than a red) and Law 9 (red is the default; no skip dressed as green); outline 9.4.2.3.3.1 and 9.4.8.1.
how: DESIGN FIRST (this is TICKETME, not built). D1 proof_coverage.teeth_printed learns a NOTRUN marker and returns {green, red, notrun}; green and red are unchanged and notrun names never join either. D2 the tester's run_proof treats a run whose teeth are all NOTRUN as 'asks for the sealer', writes no validation and prints that line, and treats a mixed run as sealing the green teeth only, listing the NOTRUN ones in evidence.stdout_tail's usual place (no ninth field). D3 (CC's decision, below). RULE 1: proof_coverage is a tool and the tester a device, so the build splits into one ticket per component. SPLIT 2026-11-14: this ticket keeps D1 (proof_coverage); the tester half is 67797b98784d.

clauses.claim: teeth_printed on output containing 'NOTRUN test_x - needs systemd' returns test_x in a notrun list and in neither green nor red, and a proof whose only tooth line is NOTRUN has an empty green list

decisions.text: D1: teeth_printed reads a NOTRUN marker into a third list; green and red unchanged. (proof_coverage)

D2: one red-first proof for clause 1 (cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_a_notrun_tooth_is_counted_neither_green_nor_red.py); proof_coverage's two whole-dict asserts over teeth_printed (cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_every_tooth_runs_and_a_red_is_named.py, cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_proof_coverage.py) gain "notrun": [], because the returned dict gains a key. The tester half (the old D2, D3 and the tester proof) is child ticket 67797b98784d, split out under RULE 1 as this ticket's HOW said.

out: the seal record's eight fields (no ninth)
converting any existing proof to print NOTRUN (a follow-up per proof: test_shim_starts_the_loop.py first)
the verdict's instrument run (9.4.8.1's bwrap-only tooth in the verdict itself), beyond using the same marker

measured.saw: proof_coverage.teeth_printed reads only the two marker sets (GREEN_MARKERS, RED_MARKERS) and returns {green, red}; device.py:736-745: verdict = GREEN if returncode == 0, then 'if verdict == GREEN and not teeth[teeth_green]: verdict = RED' with 'zero teeth printed: exit 0 with no tooth named on stdout'; grep of tester, proof_coverage, validation_store, codemother and skills found no code reading a not-run marker; the outline's 9.4.8.1 is the only mention.
measured.how: read proof_coverage.py teeth_printed and tester/device.py 726-760; grep -rniE 'not-run|not_run|notrun' over non-proof code

measured.saw: the new proof read red on origin/main (no notrun key) and green on ticket-ddc5-notrun @32744b5f9, run with plain python; two whole-dict asserts in proof_coverage's own proofs needed "notrun": []
